verdicts.flaw_description: "Each shop moved its machines to a coated carbide insert grade that quarter, and every logged run was cut on one of those machines." A tooling change that itself shortens cycle time was introduced in the same quarter and applied to every logged run, so the 4-7 minute reductions cannot be attributed to the coolant rather than the new inserts. Nothing here is blocked or held level - unlike the other controls in the report, this sentence states an uncontrolled co-intervention perfectly confounded with the treatment.

"Every stack logged here fired on a fixed duty cycle, the same hours whatever the throughput. Throughput at each site fell by half against the earlier quarter." The stated control only fixes firing HOURS; it does nothing to make particulate independent of how much material is processed. Throughput halving is an obvious alternative explanation for readings 8-14 percent lower, so the control addresses a different channel than the confounder it is placed next to.

Three of the four rows measure the outcome BEFORE the kit was issued: "issued 4 November, measured by 27 September"; "issued 5 June, measured by 28 April"; "issued 26 August, measured by 3 July". Only row Two (issued 8 January, measured by 24 March) has the measurement after the intervention. Gains recorded before the kit existed in the section cannot have been caused by it. The term labels are also inconsistent with the dates ("spring term, issued 5 June", "summer term, issued 26 August").

"Every line was stocked from a fixed year-round range, set before the period began. Premium stock's share of each store's shelf hit a record, double the earlier period." A fixed RANGE (which products are stocked) does not fix the MIX; premium stock's shelf share doubling is a direct alternative cause of a 4-7 percent rise in revenue per order, and the stated control does not block it. Secondary concern: "Figures cover the orders rung up at the new prices, and about a fifth of each line's orders were rung up at the old prices" - the current-period average excludes a fifth of orders while the month-earlier baseline includes all of them.

"Only runs completed end to end on the issued route entered the timing set, and drivers at each depot abandoned the issued route on roughly one run in six." The timing set is selected on an outcome-correlated behaviour: the runs where the new route went badly (congestion, blockages, driver override) are exactly the ones drivers abandoned, and those are excluded, while the month-earlier comparison covers all runs. The surviving one-in-six-filtered runs will show shorter times regardless of whether the routing change helps.

"Absence figures cover the pupils on the revised timetable throughout, and about a fifth of each cohort spent weeks on the old timetable." The measured group is defined by post-treatment status: a fifth of each cohort is dropped from the current figure, while the baseline ("the same cohort a term earlier") includes everyone. Pupils absent for weeks are precisely the ones who would not be on the revised timetable throughout, so excluding them mechanically lowers measured absence independent of any timetable effect.
